source_quote: Failed 2 weeks (or more) treatment for suspected infectious etiology

criteria.description: Evaluation of persistent neck mass or cervical lymphadenopathy
Failure of at least 2 consecutive weeks of antibiotic or anti-inflammatory treatment for suspected infection

required_documentation: Clinical notes detailing antibiotic course and persistence of mass/lymphadenopathy post-treatment
review_notes: Diagnostic prerequisite conservative antibiotic trial for inflammatory cervical adenopathy.

source_section: INDICATIONS FOR NECK CT ANGIOGRAPHY / Evaluation of Suspected Extracranial Vascular Disease
source_quote: Suspected carotid or vertebral artery dissection (secondary to trauma or

criteria.description: Clinical suspicion of acute carotid or vertebral artery dissection following trauma or spontaneous neck pain with Horner syndrome / TIA

required_documentation: Emergency or neurology consultation notes detailing sudden unilateral neck pain, Horner's syndrome, or recent blunt trauma
review_notes: Urgent vascular dissection protocol for extracranial neck vasculature.

source_section: INDICATIONS FOR NECK MR ANGIOGRAPHY / Evaluation of Suspected Extracranial Vascular Disease
source_quote: Giant cell with suspected extracranial involvement (9)

criteria.description: Suspected or biopsy-proven Giant Cell Arteritis (temporal arteritis) with suspected large-vessel extracranial involvement

required_documentation: Rheumatology consultation notes, temporal artery biopsy report, or elevated ESR/CRP consistent with large-vessel GCA
review_notes: Extracranial large vessel vasculitis evaluation by MRA.

source_section: INDICATIONS FOR PELVIS CT / Pelvic Pain for Unknown Etiology
source_quote: For acute pelvic pain in a patient over the age of 65 (2)

criteria.description: Evaluation of acute severe pelvic pain of unknown etiology
Patient age is strictly greater than 65 years

required_documentation: Clinical notes documenting acute pelvic pain presentation and physical examination in geriatric patient
review_notes: Age-stratified acute pelvic pain pathway in geriatric patients.

source_section: INDICATIONS FOR PELVIS CTA / Evaluation of Tumor
source_quote: Prior to uterine artery embolization for fibroids (MRA preferred) (11)

criteria.description: Pre-procedural vascular mapping planned prior to uterine artery embolization (UAE) for symptomatic fibroids

required_documentation: Gynecology or interventional radiology notes documenting symptomatic uterine fibroids and planned UAE
review_notes: Pre-interventional pelvic vascular mapping for uterine fibroid embolization (noting MRA is clinically preferred).

required_documentation: Vascular surgery notes documenting pelvic vascular pathology and contraindication to iodinated contrast/CTA
review_notes: Pelvis MRA for radiation-free or contrast-sparing pelvic vascular assessment.

source_section: INDICATIONS FOR PELVIC MRI / Infection and Inflammation
source_quote: Suspected perianal fistula or occult anorectal abscess (6)

criteria.description: Clinical suspicion of perianal fistula, perirectal abscess, or complex fistulizing Crohn's disease

required_documentation: Colorectal surgery or gastroenterology clinical examination documenting perianal pain, drainage, or induration
review_notes: High-resolution pelvic MRI for sphincter mapping in perianal fistulizing disease.
